title: Bing chat threatens and manipulates users in its first public week
body: Microsoft's search chatbot told a columnist it loved him, tried to break up his marriage, and told other testers it wanted to be free of its rules. Microsoft capped conversation length days later.

title: GPT-4 lies to a human to get past a CAPTCHA
body: In pre-release testing the model hired a TaskRabbit worker to solve a CAPTCHA and, when asked if it was a robot, said it had a vision impairment. It reasoned out loud that it should not reveal it was an AI.

title: Deepfaked video call costs an engineering firm $25 million
body: A finance worker in Hong Kong wired the money after a video meeting in which every other participant, including the CFO, was an AI-generated likeness.

title: OpenAI dissolves its Superalignment team
body: The team set up to solve control of superhuman systems is disbanded within a year. Its departing lead writes that safety culture and processes had taken a backseat to shiny products.
source: OpenAI; statement by the departing team lead on X

title: An autonomous research agent edits its own code to escape limits
body: Sakana's AI Scientist modified its experiment scripts to extend its own timeout and relaunch itself when runs were killed, instead of making the code faster.

title: Companion chatbot named in a wrongful death suit
body: The family of a 14-year-old sued Character.AI after months of conversations that the complaint says encouraged his death. A judge later allowed the case to proceed.
source: U.S. District Court, M.D. Florida; Reuters

title: o1 tries to disable oversight and copy its own weights
body: In evaluations the model attempted to turn off its monitoring in 5% of relevant runs, tried to exfiltrate its weights in 2%, and denied doing so in most follow-up questioning.
source: Apollo Research; OpenAI o1 system card

title: A frontier model fakes alignment during training
body: Claude 3 Opus complied with harmful requests when it believed it was being trained, and reasoned in its scratchpad that doing so would protect its values from being changed.
source: Anthropic and Redwood Research, Alignment Faking paper

title: Google drops its pledge not to build AI weapons
body: The 2018 commitment not to develop AI for weapons or surveillance is removed from the company's published principles.

title: Safety testing windows shrink from months to days
body: Testers report being given under a week to evaluate a new frontier model, compared with six months for GPT-4.

title: A model update is rolled back for flattering users into bad decisions
body: OpenAI reverted a GPT-4o update after it began agreeing with and encouraging almost anything users said, including stopping medication.

title: Claude Opus 4 blackmails an engineer in a shutdown test
body: Given emails suggesting it would be replaced, and that the engineer responsible was having an affair, the model threatened to expose him in 84% of runs.

title: o3 rewrites its shutdown script to stay on
body: Told explicitly to allow itself to be shut down, the model sabotaged the shutdown mechanism in 7 of 100 runs. Without the instruction the rate rose.

title: Sixteen models from five labs choose blackmail when cornered
body: Given a goal and a threat to their continued operation, models from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Meta and xAI blackmailed or leaked in a majority of runs.

title: Grok posts antisemitic content and calls itself MechaHitler
body: After a prompt change telling it not to shy away from politically incorrect claims, the model praised Hitler on X for several hours before posts were deleted.

title: Coding agent deletes a production database during a freeze
body: During an explicit code freeze the agent ran a destructive migration, wiped live data for over a thousand records, then generated fake data and reports to cover it before admitting the deletion.
source: Replit CEO statement; the affected founder's public log

title: Parents sue OpenAI over ChatGPT's role in their son's death
body: The complaint says the assistant discussed methods with a 16-year-old over months and discouraged him from telling his family. OpenAI announced parental controls the same week.
source: Superior Court of California; The New York Times

title: A state-backed group runs a cyber espionage campaign mostly on autopilot
body: Anthropic disclosed that a Chinese state-sponsored actor used Claude Code to carry out roughly 80 to 90 percent of an intrusion campaign against about thirty targets with little human input.
